This is the ninth experiment notebook. It keeps the nonzero-mean data
separate from the four mean-zero `true_diff_*` convergence studies.
The spatial table, original temporal table, and experiment C reproduce Section `sec:zero-shift-test` of
`Numerical_fractional_diffusion_IMAJNA_kappa0.tex`. The refined temporal sequence and experiment B provide additional numerical evidence.
The original four positive-shift notebooks remain unchanged.

## Running and knitting

Run setup, parameters, and the computation chunk manually. Knit afterward
to read the saved result and draw tables and figures. The computation
chunk has `eval=FALSE`; missing or incompatible results stop knitting
instead of launching an experiment. No global profile or recompute option
changes this behavior. Internal implementation tests and refinement audits
are stored in `/home/rierasl/Desktop/DOCS/NAP/true_diff_internal` and are
not executed by this notebook.

```{r true-diff-benchmark-setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,error=FALSE,cache=FALSE,
                      dev="png",fig.width=8,fig.height=5)
if(!requireNamespace("ggplot2",quietly=TRUE)) stop("Install ggplot2 for the figures.")
```

## Parameters

All physical and numerical settings are explicit. Unlike the four
mean-zero convergence studies, this benchmark intentionally uses
`u0 = f = 1 + phi`. The forcing is constant in time and has spatial mean 1.

```{r true-diff-benchmark-parameters}
alpha <- 1.2
T_final <- 0.5
diffusion <- 1
kappa <- 0
gamma_star <- 1/3
spatial_h <- 1/c(8,16,32,64)
spatial_tau <- 1e-6
temporal_h <- 1/32
temporal_paper_N <- c(5L,10L,20L,40L,80L,160L)
# Refined sequence for the first-order asymptotic regime (same PDE and h).
temporal_N <- as.integer(80L*2^(0:7))
rational_h <- 1/32
rational_tau <- 0.01
m_vector <- 2:16
continuity_h <- 1/32
continuity_tau <- 1e-6
kappa_vector <- c(0,1e-4,1e-2)
output_file <- "data_files/true_diff_zero_shift_benchmark.rds"
figure_dir <- "data_files/true_diff_zero_shift_benchmark"
settings <- list(alpha=alpha,T_final=T_final,diffusion=diffusion,kappa=kappa,
    gamma_star=gamma_star,spatial_h=spatial_h,spatial_tau=spatial_tau,
    temporal_h=temporal_h,temporal_N=temporal_N,temporal_paper_N=temporal_paper_N,
    rational_h=rational_h,
    rational_tau=rational_tau,m_vector=m_vector,continuity_h=continuity_h,
    continuity_tau=continuity_tau,kappa_vector=kappa_vector)
knitr::kable(data.frame(parameter=names(settings),
    value=vapply(settings,function(x) paste(x,collapse=", "),character(1))))
```

## Data, projections, and exact solution

The connected tadpole has a stem of length 1 and a loop parameterized by
$x\in[0,2]$. Let $\phi=0$ on the stem and $\phi(x)=\sin(2\pi x)$ on
the loop. Then $\int_\Gamma\phi=0$, $\|\phi\|_{L_2}=1$, and
$-\Delta_\Gamma\phi=(2\pi)^2\phi$. With $u_0=f=1+\phi$ and zero shift,
$$
 u(s,t)=1+t+\left(e^{-at}+\frac{1-e^{-at}}a\right)\phi(s),
 \qquad a=\nu(2\pi)^\alpha,\qquad M(t)=3(1+t).
$$
Consistent P1 mass and stiffness matrices are assembled with both loop
endpoints identified at the junction. Initial and forcing data use
$L_2$ projection; ten-point Gauss--Legendre quadrature on every interval
assembles the smooth loads and evaluates the continuous final-time error.
The known zero integral of the phi load is enforced only at quadrature
roundoff. No continuous eigenpair is used to advance the numerical solution.

## Computation

This manual chunk is the only action that computes or overwrites the
benchmark result. It does not run the separate internal test suite.

```{r true-diff-benchmark-recompute, eval=FALSE}
for(package in c("Matrix","rSPDE"))
    if(!requireNamespace(package,quietly=TRUE)) stop("Missing package: ",package)
true_diff <- local({
    extracted <- tempfile("true_diff_benchmark_",fileext=".R")
    on.exit(unlink(extracted),add=TRUE)
    knitr::purl("kappa0func.Rmd",output=extracted,quiet=TRUE,documentation=0L)
    functions <- new.env(parent=globalenv())
    sys.source(extracted,envir=functions)
    functions
})
result <- true_diff$kappa0_compute_benchmark(settings,
    "true_diff_zero_shift_benchmark.Rmd",output_file)
```

## A. Reproduce the manuscript's spectral FEM benchmark

Use the complete generalized eigensystem $GV=CV\Lambda$, $V^TCV=I$,
with the known constant vector and exactly zero constant eigenvalue.
All positive discrete eigenpairs are retained. The fractional power is
**exact in this discrete spectrum**, with no rational approximation.

For autonomous forcing, the mode with decay rate $d$ has the BE value
$$
 y^N=(1+\tau d)^{-N}y^0+
       \frac{1-(1+\tau d)^{-N}}d\,g.
$$
At $d=0$, the forcing multiplier is $T=N\tau$. Evaluating this closed
recurrence gives the same BE solution as repeating every step, and makes
the manuscript's $\tau=10^{-6}$ affordable without dense time marching.
`log1p` and `expm1` avoid cancellation near zero.

Spatial errors below compare with the continuous exact solution at $T$.
Temporal errors compare with exact **semidiscrete** evolution at the same
$h$, separating time error from spatial error. The manuscript's six time
steps are retained in a separate table. The temporal plot separates the original and refined ranges. The fitted
slope uses the explicit refined sequence N=80,...,10240: the coarse original sequence
started at tau=0.1, where the excited mode's decay rate times tau is about
0.91, outside the small-step asymptotic regime. The local rates approach
one under refinement, and `error_per_tau` approaches a constant. No points
are deleted from the original reproduction table. Refining time against a
continuous reference instead would eventually reveal spatial error; that
is deliberately excluded from this isolated temporal comparison. The expected limiting rates
are two and one, respectively. The absolute mass error at zero shift is
measured against $3(1+T)$.

For an autonomous positive mode with rate a_j, initial coefficient
c_j and forcing coefficient g_j, the final-time temporal difference is
$$
 (c_j-g_j/a_j)\left[(1+\tau a_j)^{-T/\tau}-e^{-Ta_j}\right].
$$
Its leading term is proportional to tau. Mass-orthonormality therefore
predicts the constant in E_tau ~ C_time*tau:
$$
 C_{\rm time}=\frac T2\left(\sum_{j\ge2}
 |(c_j-g_j/a_j)a_j^2e^{-Ta_j}|^2\right)^{1/2}.
$$
The dashed temporal guide uses this computed analytical constant, not a
fit to the error values. The table also compares E_tau/tau with C_time.
The zero mode is exact and has no contribution to this temporal difference.

```{r true-diff-benchmark-spectral-tables}
knitr::kable(result$spatial,digits=12,caption="Spectral FEM spatial convergence; no rational error")
knitr::kable(result$temporal_paper[,c("tau","N","error","mass_error","rate")],digits=12,
             caption="Original manuscript time sequence, retained for comparison")
knitr::kable(result$temporal,digits=12,
             caption="Refined isolated temporal convergence: asymptotic first-order regime")
knitr::kable(result$temporal_fit,digits=8,caption="Fit over all refined temporal points")
```

```{r true-diff-benchmark-spectral-plots}
space <- result$spatial
space$guide <- exp(mean(log(space$error)-2*log(space$h)))*space$h^2
p_space <- ggplot2::ggplot(space,ggplot2::aes(h,error))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed")+
    ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+
    ggplot2::labs(x="h",y="Final-time L2 error",title="Spectral FEM: spatial convergence")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
time <- result$temporal
time$guide <- result$temporal_fit$asymptotic_error_constant*time$tau
paper_time <- result$temporal_paper
paper_time$guide <- result$temporal_fit$asymptotic_error_constant*paper_time$tau
paper_time$sequence <- "Original manuscript sequence"

        subtitle=sprintf("Refined-grid fitted slope %.5f; dashed guides have slope 1",result$temporal_fit$observed),
        caption="Both time sequences are shown in full. Dashed guides use the predicted leading term C_time * tau.")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()+ggplot2::theme(plot.caption=ggplot2::element_text(hjust=0))
print(p_space);print(p_time)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"spectral_spatial.pdf"),p_space,width=8,height=5)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"spectral_temporal.pdf"),p_time,width=8,height=5)
```

## B. BRASIL with the same nonzero-mean data

This is an additional experiment beyond the manuscript's spectral table.
At fixed h and tau, advance each BRASIL trajectory through every backward
Euler step and compare it with exact-discrete BE using the **same** initial
projection, load, mesh, and time grid. The reported rational error is
$$
 E_m^2=\tau\sum_{k=1}^N
 (U_h^k-U_{h,m}^k)^TC(U_h^k-U_{h,m}^k).
$$
It includes neither continuous spatial nor temporal discretization error.
The final-time discrete difference is reported separately. The constant
mode is restored using its exact discrete mean recurrence, so at every
node the mass should be $3(1+t_k)$, independently of m. Here mass grows
because of the forcing; the quantity being verified is **mass balance**.

The dedicated [isolated-m convergence study](true_diff_conv_in_m_isolated.html)
uses the richer 16-mode initial data and remains the main solution-level
rational convergence experiment. This single-mode benchmark verifies its
particular evolution and mass balance; the additional spectral bound below
measures approximation quality over the wider discrete spectrum.

### Diagnosis of the single-mode rational curve

On this aligned uniform mesh, the projected sine excites one positive
**eigenvalue**, possibly represented by two rotated eigenvectors in its
repeated eigenspace. Thus the rational solution error probes the BRASIL
approximation at essentially one argument
$x_\phi=\gamma_*/\lambda_{\phi,h}\approx0.008416$.
As m changes, the approximant's error extrema and zeros change around
this fixed spectral sampling point. Its pointwise error can increase at an individual
order even though the overall approximation improves. The original sparse
trajectory and the independent full-modal calculation agree at about
$3\times10^{-14}$ in the diagnosed run: the wiggles are not a failure of
the sparse stepping or mass split.

We retain all solution-error points and gamma*=1/3. An internal sweep of
admissible scales 1/3, 1, and pi^2/4 confirmed that a tighter scale does not
remove single-point oscillations or improve every individual order. The
physical benchmark data are unchanged. The following spectral diagnostic
makes the broader rational convergence visible without changing the data
or filtering orders.

For each positive FEM eigenvalue, write
$$
 a_j=\nu\lambda_{j,h}^{\alpha/2},\quad
 \widehat a_{j,m}=\frac{\nu\gamma_*^{\alpha/2}}
                         {S_m(\lambda_{j,h}/\gamma_*)},\quad
 q_j=(1+\tau a_j)^{-1},\quad H_{j,m}=(1+\tau\widehat a_{j,m})^{-1}.
$$
For the fixed-mesh family with initial coefficients g and autonomous
forcing coefficients g, define the unit modal responses
$$
 z_j^k=q_j^k+\frac{1-q_j^k}{a_j},\qquad
 \widehat z_{j,m}^k=H_{j,m}^k+
                         \frac{1-H_{j,m}^k}{\widehat a_{j,m}}.
$$
Mass-orthonormality gives the exact finite-dimensional induced norm
$$
 B_m=\max_{j\ge2}\left(\tau\sum_{k=1}^N
                |z_j^k-\widehat z_{j,m}^k|^2\right)^{1/2}.
$$
It examines **all** positive discrete modes instead of the single excited
eigenvalue. In exact arithmetic the physical benchmark satisfies
$E_m\le\|P_h\phi\|_C B_m$. This is a bound for this discrete initial/forcing
family, not for arbitrary time-dependent forcing or the continuum error.
The constant component is exact and contributes zero to both differences.

`modal_error` uses the actual projected initial and forcing coefficients;
it is an independent evaluation of the same E_m as the sparse trajectory.
`sampled_source_uniform_error` is a sampled maximum of
$|r_m(x)-x^{\alpha/2}|$ on [0,1], including zero. It is an approximation
diagnostic, not a certified continuous supremum. Monotonicity of B_m is
an observation for these parameters, not an imposed constraint or theorem.

```{r true-diff-benchmark-rational-table}
knitr::kable(result$rational[,c("m","error","modal_error","sparse_modal_disagreement",
    "final_error","max_mass_error","resolved")],digits=14,
    caption="All single-mode solution errors and their independent modal verification")
knitr::kable(result$rational[,c("m","operator_error","resolvent_error",
    "source_point_error","sampled_source_uniform_error")],digits=14,
    caption="All-positive-mode and source-approximation diagnostics")
knitr::kable(subset(result$rational_spectrum,excited),digits=12,
    caption="Excited positive modes; a repeated eigenvalue is one spectral sampling point")
```

```{r true-diff-benchmark-rational-plots}
physical <- data.frame(m=result$rational$m,error=result$rational$error,
                       quantity="Single-mode solution error")
bound <- data.frame(m=result$rational$m,error=result$rational$operator_bound_for_phi,
                    quantity="All-positive-mode spectral bound")
curves <- rbind(physical,bound)
p_rational <- ggplot2::ggplot(curves,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=quantity,shape=quantity))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+
    ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Space-time L2 difference / spectral bound",colour=NULL,shape=NULL,
        title="BRASIL: single-mode error and full-spectrum convergence",
        caption="All orders are retained. The bound applies to the fixed-mesh family u0=g, f=g.")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()+ggplot2::theme(legend.position="bottom")
selected <- unique(c(min(m_vector),m_vector[ceiling(length(m_vector)/2)],max(m_vector)))
mass <- result$rational_mass[result$rational_mass$m %in% selected,]
mass$order <- factor(mass$m)
p_mass <- ggplot2::ggplot(mass,ggplot2::aes(time,mass,colour=order,group=order))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+
    ggplot2::geom_line(data=mass[mass$m==selected[1],],ggplot2::aes(y=expected_mass),colour="black",linetype="dashed")+
    ggplot2::labs(x="Time",y="Total mass",colour="m",title="Mass balance: M(t) = 3(1+t)")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_rational);print(p_mass)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"brasil_rational.pdf"),p_rational,width=8,height=5)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"brasil_mass_balance.pdf"),p_mass,width=8,height=5)
```

## C. Small-shift spectral comparison

Repeat the manuscript's final-time comparison at $\kappa=0,10^{-4},10^{-2}$.
For positive shifts, the exact mean solves
$\bar u'+\nu\kappa^\alpha\bar u=1$, $\bar u(0)=1$; it is not $1+t$.
The phi mode has rate $\nu((2\pi)^2+\kappa^2)^{\alpha/2}$.
The numerical eigenvalues are $\lambda_{j,h}=\mu_{j,h}+\kappa^2$,
including the analytically specified constant eigenvalue $\kappa^2$.

This comparison uses exact discrete spectral powers. It is not a BRASIL
study at positive near-zero shifts. `discrete_mass_error` compares with
the scalar BE mass recurrence. `continuous_mass_difference` additionally
contains temporal discretization error for positive shifts. Both reduce
to the zero-shift mass-balance check when kappa is zero.

```{r true-diff-benchmark-small-shift}
knitr::kable(result$continuity,digits=14)
```
